requirements.quote: `bin/lean/ci-classify.mjs` (new) — `classifyCiFailure({step, lines, test, flakes})` → `{class, signature, downstream}` with classes `deterministic-setup` (command not found, missing module/package, npm/pnpm config/ERESOLVE, lockfile mismatch, image pull/manifest unknown, permission denied on setup paths), `generated-artifact-stale` (diff-after-generate / "out of date, run X" / drift checks), `infra` (reuse `INFRA_SIGNATURES`), `flaky-suspect` (signature present in the flake ledger via `release-flakes.mjs` `readFlakes`/`signatureHash`), `code` (test assertion/type/lint error otherwise).
`downstream: true` for setup and stale classes.
`bin/pool/ci-events.mjs` — classify `step_failed`/`test_failed` on ingest when the event has no `class`.
`failFastDecision(event, policy)`; policy `fail_fast: off|deterministic` (default off); only `deterministic-setup`/`generated-artifact-stale` may return `cancel`.
Cancelling itself is done by the subscriber (#5687 lane consumer), never by the router.
`bin/lean/release-flakes.mjs` — export what the classifier reuses; no behaviour change.
`bin/lean/ci-classify.test.mjs` (new) with a fixture corpus of ≥ 40 real-shaped failure excerpts (≥ 5 per class, multi-ecosystem: node, python, go, docker); devdocs entry.
Fixture corpus accuracy ≥ 90% overall and 100% on `deterministic-setup` precision (no `code` failure ever classed as setup), table printed by the test and recorded in the PR [type:unit]
`failFastDecision` returns `cancel` only for downstream classes and only when policy is `deterministic`; `flaky-suspect`, `code`, `infra` never cancel [type:unit]

requirements.why: fail_fast ships default off; enabling it needs a first cohort, guard metrics (false-cancel rate on deterministic classes) and shadow evidence from the #5687 lane consumer, which is separate work

deliverables.change: New pure module: classifyCiFailure (ordered regex tables; precedence setup > stale > infra (INFRA_SIGNATURES) > flake-ledger hit via signatureHash > code; flake override only applies to a would-be code result; downstream true for setup/stale) and failFastDecision (cancel only for downstream classes under policy fail_fast==='deterministic'; default off).
createCiEvents accepts optional injected classify and flakes getter; ingest stays synchronous and sets class on step_failed/test_failed events lacking one. Router never cancels.
Only if something the classifier reuses is not already exported (INFRA_SIGNATURES, signatureHash, readFlakes are); otherwise untouched. No behaviour change.

New: corpus of at least 40 excerpts (at least 5 per class; node, python, go, docker), prints accuracy table, asserts >=90% overall and 100% setup precision; failFastDecision matrix; flake-ledger override; downstream flag.
Add ingest tests: class set when absent on step_failed/test_failed, preserved when supplied, untouched for other event types.
Document the classifier, the ingest hook, the fail_fast policy (default off) and that cancelling belongs to the subscriber.
Add a short ci-classify.mjs entry next to the ci-preflight paragraph.

preserve.what: release-flakes.mjs exports and classifyFailure behaviour (bin/lean/release-flakes.mjs:39), exercised by bin/lean/release-flakes.test.mjs unchanged
ci-events validateEvent contract, ingest return shape {accepted, seq}, ring/NDJSON behaviour (bin/pool/ci-events.mjs:28-162), exercised by bin/pool/ci-events.test.mjs
Router endpoints /ci/events behaviour (bin/pool/router.mjs); the router does not gain cancel logic

regression.covers: release-flakes consumers (release.mjs rerunInfraFlakes) and ci-events ingest callers

decisions.choice: Classifier is a pure function taking flakes as an argument; the pool injects the classifier and flakes getter rather than reading the ledger
decisions.justification: ingest is synchronous (bin/pool/ci-events.mjs:150) while readFlakes is async and needs a lane context (bin/lean/release-flakes.mjs:139); keeps pool free of lean ledger I/O

decisions.choice: Flake-ledger hit overrides only a would-be code result, not setup/stale/infra
decisions.justification: Issue says the hit overrides code; 100% setup precision and never-cancel-on-flaky require setup patterns to win
